section: Andhra region under the Company - Machilipatnam, Ceded Districts, early administration and revenue
subsections: Collectorates/districts - formation, Masulipatnam Council, Committee of Circuit

accepted.s: The earliest establishment of a Dutch factory at Machilipatnam is associated with which year?
accepted.x: The Dutch established a factory at Machilipatnam in 1605, while the English factory there dates to 1611.
accepted.tq: Use the exact year in a close chronological pair.
accepted.sec: Chronology of Andhra colonial events  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the action of Salabat Jung in 1759?
o: He introduced the Permanent Settlement in Andhra.
He transferred Guntur and Nellore to the British.
He gave Machilipatnam and Nizampatnam to the British.
He divided the Ceded Districts into Bellary and Cuddapah.
accepted.x: In 1759, Salabat Jung gave Machilipatnam and Nizampatnam to the British.
accepted.tq: Test the ruler–event association and reject swapped administrative events.
accepted.sec: Chronology of Andhra colonial events  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Shah Alam II issued the firman relating to the Northern Circars in 1765.
2. The Northern Circars were transferred under a treaty in 1766.
3. The Treaty of Masulipatnam settled the dispute in 1768.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the firman was issued in 1765, the treaty transferring the Circars was concluded in 1766, and the Treaty of Masulipatnam settled the dispute in 1768.
accepted.tq: Link successive constitutional and political events in a dated sequence.
accepted.sec: Chronology of Andhra colonial events  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following events occurred in 1788?
o: Guntur was acquired or handed over to the British.
The Ceded Districts were divided into Bellary and Cuddapah.
The Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam was concluded.
The Permanent Settlement was applied in Andhra.
accepted.x: Guntur was acquired or handed over to the British in 1788.
accepted.tq: Identify the event attached to a single year.
accepted.sec: Chronology of Andhra colonial events  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam
B. Guntur handed over to the British
C. Treaty of Masulipatnam
D. Battle of Padmanabham
accepted.x: The correct order is Treaty of Masulipatnam (1768), Guntur handed over (1788), Battle of Padmanabham (1794), and Subsidiary Alliance (1798).
accepted.tq: Arrange events by their dates, beginning with the earliest sure event.
accepted.sec: Chronology of Andhra colonial events  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam was concluded in:
accepted.x: The Nizam entered into the Subsidiary Alliance with the British in 1798.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a diplomatic event from nearby territorial settlements.
accepted.sec: Chronology of Andhra colonial events  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. 1794 — Battle of Padmanabham
2. 1800 — Ceded Districts obtained from the Nizam
3. 1801 — Nellore and Chittoor annexed
4. 1802 — Ryotwari introduced in the Ceded Districts
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. These events occurred in 1794, 1800, 1801 and 1802 respectively.
accepted.tq: Check each year–event pair rather than relying on one familiar date.
accepted.sec: Chronology of Andhra colonial events  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who was appointed Principal Collector of the Ceded Districts in 1800?
accepted.x: Thomas Munro was appointed Principal Collector when the Ceded Districts were obtained from the Nizam in 1800.
accepted.tq: Use the administrator–appointment association.
accepted.sec: Chronology of Andhra colonial events  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Ceded Districts were divided into Bellary and Cuddapah in:
accepted.x: The Ceded Territory was divided into the districts of Bellary and Cuddapah in 1808.
accepted.tq: Separate the date of acquisition from the date of territorial division.
accepted.sec: Chronology of Andhra colonial events  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: West Godavari was created in 1925, not 1911. Kurnool, Anantapur, and Guntur with East Godavari were associated with 1858, 1882, and 1904 respectively.
accepted.tq: Find the one incorrect district-formation year.
accepted.sec: Collectorates/districts - formation, Masulipatnam Council, Committee of Circuit  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The name ‘Rayalaseema’ was adopted in:
accepted.x: The name Rayalaseema was adopted in 1928.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two close years associated with the same regional development.
accepted.sec: Chronology of Andhra colonial events  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which one of the following was the correct sequence of the four events?
A. Ryotwari extended across Madras
B. Abolition of zamindari in Madras
C. Guntur handed over to the British
D. Battle of Padmanabham
accepted.x: The events occurred in 1788, 1794, 1820 and 1948 respectively: Guntur, Padmanabham, extension of Ryotwari, and abolition of zamindari.
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest and latest dates.
accepted.sec: Chronology of Andhra colonial events  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Before the Northern Circars were acquired, the East India Company’s factories in the region were located at:
accepted.x: Before acquiring the Circars, the East India Company maintained factories at Machilipatnam and Visakhapatnam.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct pair of early Company centres.
accepted.sec: Collectorates/districts - formation, Masulipatnam Council, Committee of Circuit  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Until the abolition of the Board of Revenue, the Northern Circars were governed by a:
accepted.x: The Northern Circars were governed by a Chief-in-Council at Masulipatnam until the earlier administrative arrangement was replaced.
accepted.tq: Match the administrative institution with its headquarters.
accepted.sec: Collectorates/districts - formation, Masulipatnam Council, Committee of Circuit  [APPSC]

accepted.s: What was the principal recommendation of the Committee of Circuit regarding the Circars’ revenue administration?
o: Revenue rights should be granted permanently to the Nizam.
Revenue rights should not be auctioned.
Revenue collection should be transferred to village panchayats.
Revenue rights should be auctioned annually.
accepted.x: The Committee of Circuit reviewed revenue administration and advised against auctioning revenue rights.
accepted.tq: Identify the policy recommendation from the committee’s stated function.
accepted.sec: Collectorates/districts - formation, Masulipatnam Council, Committee of Circuit  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the five coastal collectorates?
accepted.x: The five coastal collectorates were Ganjam, Visakhapatnam, Godavari, Krishna and Nellore. Kurnool belonged to the Ceded Territory.
accepted.tq: Separate coastal districts from Ceded Territory districts.
accepted.sec: Collectorates/districts - formation, Masulipatnam Council, Committee of Circuit  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The headquarters of the Krishna collectorate was at:
accepted.x: The Krishna collectorate was headquartered at Machilipatnam.
accepted.tq: Use the district–headquarters association.
accepted.sec: Collectorates/districts - formation, Masulipatnam Council, Committee of Circuit  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the Ceded Territory, the four sub-collectors were stationed at Harpanahalli, Kadapa, Adoni and:
accepted.x: The four sub-collectorates were Harpanahalli, Kadapa, Adoni and Kurnool.
accepted.tq: Complete a location list using the nearby administrative units.
accepted.sec: Collectorates/districts - formation, Masulipatnam Council, Committee of Circuit  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the functions of the District Collector from 1794?
o: Judicial administration without any revenue responsibility
Collection of land revenue, maintenance of law and order, and magisterial duties
accepted.x: The Collector was responsible for land revenue, law and order, and acted as District Magistrate or Judge.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing the complete set of administrative functions.
accepted.sec: Collectorates/districts - formation, Masulipatnam Council, Committee of Circuit  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The judicial powers of the District Collector were taken away in:
accepted.x: The Collector’s judicial powers were withdrawn in 1816, although revenue and administrative responsibilities continued.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the beginning of an office from the later alteration of its powers.
accepted.sec: Collectorates/districts - formation, Masulipatnam Council, Committee of Circuit  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the initial collectorates of the Andhra region:
1. Ganjam was one of them.
2. Bellary was one of them.
3. Kurnool was one of them.
4. Chittoor was one of them.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The initial eight collectorates included Ganjam, Bellary and Kurnool, but not Chittoor. Chittoor was formed later in 1911.
accepted.tq: Test membership in a historically specific administrative list.
accepted.sec: Collectorates/districts - formation, Masulipatnam Council, Committee of Circuit  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Permanent Settlement replaced the earlier practice of auctioning zamindaris with:
o: A tax collected only from artisans
accepted.x: The Permanent Settlement introduced a fixed revenue demand in place of the auctioning of zamindaris.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the reform measure from unrelated revenue practices.
accepted.sec: Revenue terms and taxes - Moturpha, peshkash, Haveli  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Permanent Settlement was introduced by Cornwallis in 1793 and applied in Andhra in:
accepted.x: Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement in 1793, and it was applied in Andhra in 1802.
accepted.tq: Separate the year of introduction from the year of regional application.
accepted.sec: Revenue terms and taxes - Moturpha, peshkash, Haveli  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the revenue systems applied in Andhra?
o: Permanent Settlement was applied in the Ceded Districts and Ryotwari in coastal Andhra.
Ryotwari was applied in the Ceded Districts and Permanent Settlement in Andhra’s zamindari areas.
Both systems were applied only in the Ceded Districts.
accepted.x: Permanent Settlement was applied in Andhra in 1802, while Ryotwari was applied in the Ceded Districts.
accepted.tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap between two revenue systems.
accepted.sec: Revenue terms and taxes - Moturpha, peshkash, Haveli  [APPSC]

accepted.s: ‘Peshkash’ refers to:
o: The share of revenue paid by zamindars to the British
Revenue collected by zamindars from farmers
accepted.x: Peshkash was the share of revenue paid by zamindars to the British.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among closely related colonial revenue terms.
accepted.sec: Revenue terms and taxes - Moturpha, peshkash, Haveli  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Haveli lands in coastal Andhra were lands:
o: Assigned to the Nizam as military grants
accepted.x: Haveli lands were under the direct control of the British in coastal Andhra.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact ownership or control category.
accepted.sec: Revenue terms and taxes - Moturpha, peshkash, Haveli  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the arrangement relating to zamindari lands, which proportion of the estimated revenue went to the government?
accepted.x: Nine-tenths of the estimated revenue went to the government and one-tenth went to the zamindar.
accepted.tq: Test the precise numerical proportion rather than the general arrangement.
accepted.sec: Revenue terms and taxes - Moturpha, peshkash, Haveli  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The agreements relating to zamindari revenue were generally made for a period of:
accepted.x: The agreements relating to zamindari lands ran for ten years.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact duration attached to the revenue agreement.
accepted.sec: Revenue terms and taxes - Moturpha, peshkash, Haveli  [APPSC]
